name: Honora Greywick
languages: French (a governess, then a summer in Paris she has never stopped talking about)
equipment: Heavy coat: a long grey wool walking coat with deep pockets, a silk mourning band on the sleeve
Pocket revolver (.32, five-shot), her father's, taken from his desk drawer on Sunday without asking anyone
Walking stick of ash with a brass ferrule, for the bluff paths
A box camera loaded for a hundred exposures, and a leather case for it
A pocket notebook ruled for observations, two pencils and a pocket lens
A brass pocket thermometer from the college observatory, for measuring cold spots, which she insists are draughts
A letter from the observatory director offering her a paid assistant's post from January, if she can afford to live on $300 a year
A tin of Pastilles and a box of matches
features: There's an Explanation (Skeptic: once per short rest, when you fail a fear check, name a rational cause aloud, in character, and the failure becomes a success with no Dread; the explanation need not be true. Advantage on Investigation to find the mechanism behind anything that is not supernatural, and after 10 minutes searching a room the GM says whether any part of what is happening in it is a person's doing)

Careful Notes (Skeptic: once per short rest, after 10 minutes examining a scene, ask what here has been moved, who was here most recently, or what here does not fit, and get a true answer; it never names a creature's rule outright)

Calm Explanation (Skeptic, 2nd level: once per long rest, as an action, explain a frightening phenomenon to allies who can hear you; until the end of the scene they have advantage on fear checks against that one horror)

The Family Name (Old Family origin: advantage on Persuasion with the propertied, professional and old families; once per scenario an introduction, letter or meeting with someone of standing without a check; you know without a check the reputation and well-known scandals of prominent local families; old grudges come with the name)

Library Privileges (Student background: she can get into any academic library and most private ones, a professor will see her about their subject, and people explain things to her in more detail than they would to anyone else, which she finds infuriating and useful)

personality.traits: I measure things. Temperature, distance, time, the length of a silence. I say exactly what I think and then explain why it is reasonable. I am kinder than I sound, and I sound like a schoolmistress.
personality.ideals: Everything has a cause. If I cannot find it, I have not looked hard enough. A woman can do science as well as any man and will have to do it better to be allowed.
personality.bonds: Linus, my younger brother, who wrote to me every week from Chicago and has not written since the eighth. My father, whom I loved and did not understand. The college observatory and the post I have been offered there.
personality.flaws: I have explained away one thing in this house for seven years, and if I stop explaining it I do not know what I will be. I am contemptuous of Conrad and polite to Leonora, and I have never asked myself whether either is fair.

appearance: A tall, thin, upright woman of twenty-seven with her father's grey river eyes, dark hair pinned up hard under a small black hat, wire spectacles she pushes up her nose when she is thinking, ink on her right forefinger, and a way of standing with her hands clasped behind her back like a lecturer. Black silk for mourning, a grey walking coat over it, sensible boots.
backstory: Honora Greywick was born in Greywick House in 1866, the youngest of Jasper Greywick's three children by his first wife, Caroline, who died when Honora was four. Leonora came when she was seven. She grew up in the Tower Room with a telescope her father bought her and a window that looked north along the house to the stone wing, and every night of her childhood she watched Mrs. Quell carry a lamp up into a room nobody used. Nobody would tell her why. So she decided it was nonsense, and went to Vassar College in Poughkeepsie, graduated in astronomy in 1888, and has worked since as an unpaid computer at the college observatory, reducing other people's observations by lamplight. In October 1886, home for the autumn and furious with Leonora over something she has forgotten, she locked her bedroom door for the first and only time in her life, and at three in the morning she woke to the handle turning and a slow scratching at the bottom of the door; her father broke the door in at a quarter to three, white as paper, and held her and would not say why. She has explained it to herself for seven years: a rat, a dream, her father's nerves. She is named in the will for a fifth of the residue, which would let her take the observatory post and never marry anyone for money, which is what she wants most in the world. On Sunday night, at three, she heard Linus call her name through the north wing door, and she is not explaining that away. (Hooks: Linus's voice; the lamp; her own locked door in 1886; she is Greywick blood and can say the name in the rite. Suggested ally: Dr. Wyle, who brought her into the world.)
